## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0706ba39cd32355a15d61ecf8aee8d8619a59e57`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #12992 (body, triage `6255678074`, claim `6256076833`, os-dev-report `6256244967`), PR #13001 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main` `4dfdebdf5f`), the 35 check-runs on the head, and the base tree's `packages/react/src/index.ts`, `packages/react/README.md`, `scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs` header, `packages/react/src/hooks/useExpression.ts`, `packages/react/src/hooks/usePageVariables.tsx` and `AGENTS.md` (read only).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public-surface change: exactly one symbol, and it is the one the PR names.** The diff adds one `export` keyword in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` (`export function buildNodeEvaluationScope`). `packages/react/src/index.ts` is untouched and already carries `export * from './SchemaRenderer.js'`, so the function is reachable from the `@object-ui/react` entry with no index line. Nothing else becomes reachable: the removed `const configEvaluationScope` was module-private, no other declaration gains or loses `export`, and `@object-ui/components` adds only an import. The new pin `buildNodeEvaluationScope-12992.test.ts` imports from `../index`, which holds the entry claim. **Right.**

2. **Existing callers see byte-identical behaviour.** The arrow `configEvaluationScope` became a function declaration returning the same object literal: `...predicateScope`, `current_user: predicateScope?.user`, the conditional `{ record: boundRecord }` spread guarded by `boundRecord && typeof boundRecord === 'object' && !Array.isArray(boundRecord)`, then `page: pageVariables`. Both existing call sites (`SchemaRenderer`'s evaluation memo and `evaluateConfigBagInScope`) pass the same three arguments in the same order. The declaration-vs-const change is immaterial (both callers sit below it in the module). **Right.**

3. **`isItemVisible` scope: same key SET and same value per key; insertion order differs.** Old literal: `{ ...row(if object), ...predicateScope, current_user: predicateScope?.user, record: row, data: row, page: pageVariables }`. New: `{ ...row(if object), ...buildNodeEvaluationScope(predicateScope, row, pageVariables), record: row, data: row }`. Walking it: the flat-row spread is unchanged (still `typeof === 'object'` with no array guard, so an array row still spreads its indices, as before); the builder spreads `predicateScope`, writes `current_user`, conditionally writes `record`, writes `page`; then `record` and `data` are set to the row unconditionally, so when the row is not a non-array object the ambient `record` the builder preserved is overwritten with the row (`undefined`, `null`, a string, an array), which is exactly what the old literal did. Every key resolves to the same value. What is not identical is property insertion order (old `…, current_user, record, data, page`; new `…, current_user, [record], page, record, data`). `ExpressionEvaluator` resolves scope roots by property lookup, not by enumeration, so this is not observable to a predicate. The PR body's "key-for-key" claim is true of set and values; I note the order difference so nobody later reads "identical" as "byte-identical object". **Right, with that note.**

4. **Badge gates' scope is identical to the old inline mirror.** The removed literal was the builder's body verbatim (same spread order, same `!Array.isArray` guard, same `page`), with `(predicateScope as any)?.user` in place of `predicateScope?.user`, which is the same value. Both callers of the builder pass `usePredicateScope()` (typed `Record (string to any)`, assignable to `Record (string to unknown)`), `useRecordContext().data`, and `usePageVariables().variables` (the variables map, not the context object, in both `SchemaRenderer` and `containers.tsx`). **Right.**

5. **Exported name and signature are a sound published contract.** `buildNodeEvaluationScope(predicateScope: Record (string to unknown), boundRecord: unknown, pageVariables: unknown): Record (string to unknown)`: fully typed, no `any` on the face, the two permissive parameters are deliberately `unknown` because the function itself guards `boundRecord`. The JSDoc names the four roots in the order they are written and describes each correctly: root 3's "a `record` the ambient scope supplies is not shadowed by an empty one; a row, written after the spread, wins" is exactly the conditional spread; root 4's "`PageSchema.variables` as `page.VAR`" matches what both callers pass. One caller-specific phrase: root 1's parenthetical "plus a node's API-bound `data` once it has answered" describes what `SchemaRenderer` puts into `predicateScope`, not something the builder does; the sentence is framed as "every root `predicateScope` carries", so it is accurate as a description of the input, and the badge caller's narrower input is the dev's second out-of-scope note (③). The name is broader than `visibleWhen` on purpose and the PR body justifies it (the same scope evaluates `properties`, `content`, and action-container members via `evaluateConfigBagInScope`). The JSDoc ships into the `.d.ts`, so the published surface is self-describing. **Right.**

6. **README omission: not a defect this PR must fix before landing; it is a docs follow-up.** `AGENTS.md` #2 ("Docs-driven. For every feature/refactor, update package `README.md` and `content/docs/guide/*.md`. Not done until docs reflect the code.") is the rule the dev cites, and read literally a new public function in `@object-ui/react` should appear in `packages/react/README.md`. Against that: (i) the only mechanized gate on READMEs, `check:readme-exports` (`scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs`, run by `repo-gates.yml`), judges in the opposite direction, "every name a README imports FROM ITS OWN PACKAGE must be a name that package really exports"; an undocumented export cannot fail it, so there is no CI verdict to cite, and the `Repo Gates` run that carries it is still `in_progress` on this head; (ii) the react README today is not an export index: it has no section for `evaluateConfigBagInScope`, `usePredicateScope`, `usePageVariables` or `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate` either, and its "API Reference" heading defers to the site; (iii) the scope's semantics (`current_user`, `record`, `page`) are already documented in `content/docs/guide/expressions.md` and `schema-rendering.md` and are unchanged by this PR; (iv) the changeset body states the signature and the four roots, so the CHANGELOG will document the contract; (v) the claim comment's file surface excluded the README and the dev stopped at the boundary as ordered. The sibling PR objectui#12949 added a README section for a new public prop, and that is the better practice; the difference is that a prop on an authoring face is user-facing metadata, while this export exists for one in-repo consumer. Verdict: acceptable to land; the seat should either ask the dev for a short README section (a `buildNodeEvaluationScope` heading, signature plus the four roots, under "Hooks"/utilities) in this PR as a no-cost nicety, or carry it as an Acceptance note (③). Not a PASS/FAIL condition.

7. **Card's "Done when" is met as far as the card's own words allow.** "`containers.tsx` builds no scope of its own; both readers call the one builder; the #12987 pins stay green." The badge gates build no scope; the item-level `isItemVisible` composes the builder and then adds its own breadth (flat row, unconditional `record`/`data`), which the claim's "⛔ No change to what the scope contains" ordered the dev to preserve. The dev's premise note is right: the triage comment's `:664-690` range points at `isItemVisible`, the card body describes the badge mirror; both are now served by the one builder. The #12987 pin file is unchanged in the diff and the dev reports it green (CI test shards still in progress, see below).

8. **Check-runs on `0706ba39cd`** (the gate verdicts, read at review time): `success`: Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Overwrite Report, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Line Citation Gate, Test (dist pins), Build & E2E, Live E2E (informational), label. `skipped`: dependabot, Test (coverage), Test (coverage shard). `in_progress` at review time: Repo Gates (carries `check:readme-exports`), Type Check, Lint, Build Docs, Bundle Analysis, Test shards 1/16 through 16/16. No failure recorded. The in-progress families are the ones the dev declared to CI (full-directory test runs, lint, type-check); the adopting seat should re-read them before merge. This record does not wait on them.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/12992-visiblewhen-scope-builder.md`: `@object-ui/react: minor`, `@object-ui/components: patch`. **Matches what the diff publishes.** `@object-ui/react` gains a new exported function at its entry, an additive widening of a published surface: `minor` under this repo's policy (`AGENTS.md` §版本号策略: minor/patch evolve independently of `@objectstack`; `major` is never declared in a changeset and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces it, green here as `Changeset Bump Policy`). `@object-ui/components` changes only the internal construction of two evaluators with no root change and no export change: `patch`, and the published-source rule in AGENTS.md (any `src/` change in a `fixed`-group package needs a changeset) is satisfied; `Changeset Declaration` / `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are green. The body makes no claim the diff does not back ("No root changes for any caller" is what ① items 2-4 found). `Clause-②: yes` on the PR is correct: a symbol newly reachable from a package entry is the clause's definition, and the card and the claim both forecast it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev deviation 1 (index.ts not edited): correct, `export *` already covers it; the entry pin holds the claim.
- Dev deviation 2 (whole-directory runs declared to CI): the directory families are the in-progress Test shards / Lint / Type Check on this head; no local re-run by this review.
- Dev deviation 3 (`isItemVisible` composed too): judged in ① item 3; values unchanged, within the claim's "no change to what the scope contains".
- Dev deviation 4 (attribution trailer): not a contract matter; noted for the seat.
- Out-of-scope note 1 (`packages/react/README.md` lacks the new export): **Acceptance notes**, not file-worthy. It is none of the three classes (no public door giving a wrong answer, no named producer, no security/release-text/maintainer exception); the README gate cannot fire on it; the changeset documents the contract. Recommended disposition: ask the dev to add the section in this PR if the seat wants it closed now; otherwise carry as an Acceptance note with dedupe words `buildNodeEvaluationScope README`.
- Out-of-scope note 2 (badge gates evaluate over the ambient predicate scope, without a gated node's API-bound `data` that `SchemaRenderer` adds once the binding answers): **Acceptance notes on today's evidence**, pre-existing since #12991 and unchanged by this PR (the builder spreads whatever `predicateScope` it is given; the difference is in what the badge caller passes, not in the builder). The dev read it from code and measured no public entry point. It becomes class a (public door + wrong answer) only if a gated node on a related list's path also has its own API `dataSource` binding and its `visibleWhen` reads `data.*`; in that case the badge's `evaluateCondition` would see `data` unresolved and fail open while the body's gate could close once the binding answers, so the strip could count a list the body hides. That is a real divergence shape but unmeasured; escalate as an Acceptance note with the condition stated, and file as class a only on a measured reproduction. Dedupe words: `page:tabs gate api data`, `visibleWhen data root badge`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-12992-visiblewhen-scope-builder`
Reviewed-by: `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`

**VERDICT: PASS**
